$comment: Receipts for every number this book repository publishes in prose: the 14 chapter files, the README's status column and five-part 目录, the hero figure's legend and ladder, and the papers list's per-chapter coverage. Each check re-derives the figure from the committed Markdown/SVG with python3 (standard library only, offline); none of them echoes a constant that is also written here.

claims.claim: The book is planned as 14 chapters, one committed file per chapter.
claims.method: glob over the committed chapters/ directory; no index file can disagree with the filesystem

claims.claim: The README's status column (✅ written / 🚧 outline) agrees with what the chapter files actually contain: a file still ending in `*本章待展开。*` is an outline, a file without that line is written.
claims.metric: each README chapter row's status marker compared with the presence of the `本章待展开` line in the file it links to
claims.method: parse the README table rows, then for every row require marker ✅ ⟺ the linked chapters/*.md does not contain 本章待展开
claims.repro: grep -L 本章待展开 chapters/*.md  # the two that come back are the ✅ rows

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io;T="".join(map(chr,[0x672c,0x7ae0,0x5f85,0x5c55,0x5f00]));D=chr(0x2705);rows=[(l.split("](")[1].split(")")[0],l.rstrip().split("|")[-2].strip()) for l in io.open("README.md",encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines() if l.startswith("| [") and "](" in l and l.count("|")>=4];rows=[r for r in rows if r[0].startswith("chapters/")];w=sum(1 for p,s in rows if s==D);bad=sum(1 for p,s in rows if ((T in io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read())!=(s!=D)));print("rows",len(rows),"written",w,"outline",len(rows)-w,"mismatched",bad)'

claims.claim: The hero figure's legend ('已成稿 2 章' / '共 14 章') and its ladder (14 rungs, the first 2 bronze, the rest outline) count the same chapters the repository ships.
claims.value: ladder 14 rungs (2 bronze + 12 outline), legend [2, 14], files 14, written 2
claims.metric: rungs in the hero SVG's `rungs` group by fill colour, legend numbers read from the SVG's own legend text, written/total re-derived from chapters/*.md
claims.method: count <rect> in assets/readme/hero.svg's `rungs` group by fill (#B9862F written, #E9E0CE outline), read the two legend numbers, and re-derive the same two counts from chapters/*.md

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,glob,re;T="".join(map(chr,[0x672c,0x7ae0,0x5f85,0x5c55,0x5f00]));f=sorted(glob.glob("chapters/*.md"));w=sum(1 for p in f if T not in io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read());h=io.open("assets/readme/hero.svg",encoding="utf-8").read();r=h.split("id=\"rungs\"")[1].split("</g>")[0];leg=re.findall("<text[^>]*>([^<]*)</text>",h.split("id=\"legend\"")[1].split("</g>")[0]);n=[int(re.findall("[0-9]+",t)[0]) for t in leg];print("rungs",r.count("<rect"),"bronze",r.count("#B9862F"),"outline",r.count("#E9E0CE"),"legend",n,"files",len(f),"written",w)'

expect.equals: rungs 14 bronze 2 outline 12 legend [2, 14] files 14 written 2

claims.claim: `references/papers.md` is organised by chapter, recommends 2–3 must-read papers per chapter section, and has no section for chapter 4 or chapter 13 (the file says so in its opening line).
claims.value: 11 sections / 25 papers / 2–3 per section / every chapter except 4 and 13 has a section (12 of 14)
claims.metric: sections (`##` headings) and their bullet links in references/papers.md; chapter numbers parsed out of each section heading
claims.method: split the file on `## ` headings, count `- [` bullets per section, union the chapter numbers named in the headings, and list chapters 1–14 with no section

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,re;p=io.open("references/papers.md",encoding="utf-8").read();sec=re.split(r"^## ",p,flags=re.M)[1:];cnt=[len(re.findall(r"^- \[",s,re.M)) for s in sec];cov=sorted({int(n) for s in sec for n in re.findall("[0-9]+",s.split(chr(10))[0])});print("sections",len(sec),"papers",sum(cnt),"per-section",min(cnt),max(cnt),"chapters-covered",len(cov),"no-section",[c for c in range(1,15) if c not in cov])'

claims.claim: `SUMMARY.md` lists all 14 chapters plus the two appendix files, and every relative link in `SUMMARY.md` and `README.md` points at a file that exists in the checkout.
claims.value: 17 links in SUMMARY.md, 14 of them chapters, 0 missing, 0 chapter files unlisted
claims.metric: relative links extracted from SUMMARY.md and README.md and resolved against the working tree; chapters/*.md not referenced by SUMMARY.md counted
claims.method: pull `](...)` targets out of SUMMARY.md and README.md, stat each relative one, and diff the SUMMARY chapter links against chapters/*.md

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,re,glob,os;L=lambda f: re.findall(r"\]\(([^)]+)\)",io.open(f,encoding="utf-8").read());s=L("SUMMARY.md");all_=s+L("README.md");loc=[l for l in all_ if not l.startswith("http") and not l.startswith("#")];miss=sorted({l for l in loc if not os.path.exists(l.split("#")[0])});ch=[l for l in s if l.startswith("chapters/")];files=sorted(glob.glob("chapters/*.md"));print("summary-links",len(s),"summary-chapters",len(ch),"missing",len(miss),"files-not-listed",len([f for f in files if f not in ch]))'

claims.claim: The README blurb — 已规划五部分共 14 章 — and its 目录 split the book into five parts holding 4+2+3+2+3 chapters, one row per chapter file (the written/outline split in the same blurb is receipted by readme-status-column-matches-files).
claims.metric: `###` part headings in README.md and the chapter rows under each
claims.method: split README.md on `###` headings, keep the five that name a 部分, count their `| [第` rows

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,re;r=io.open("README.md",encoding="utf-8").read();P="".join(map(chr,[0x90e8,0x5206]));b=[x for x in re.split(r"^### ",r,flags=re.M)[1:] if P in x.split(chr(10))[0]];c=[len(re.findall(r"^\| \[",x,re.M)) for x in b];print("parts",len(b),"chapters-per-part",c,"total",sum(c))'

claims.claim: The README's 如何使用 step 2 — 第 1-2 章末尾有思考题，其余章节待补 — is what the files show: exactly the two written chapters have a 思考题 section.
claims.value: 2 chapters with a 思考题 section, none of them an outline
claims.metric: files under chapters/ containing an `## 思考题` heading
claims.method: scan chapters/*.md for the `## 思考题` heading and list the files that have it
claims.evidence: chapters/ch01-what-is-agent.md + chapters/ch02-harness.md (README 如何使用 step 2)

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,glob;Q="".join(map(chr,[0x601d,0x8003,0x9898]));f=sorted(glob.glob("chapters/*.md"));h=[p.split("/")[-1] for p in f if ("## "+Q) in io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read()];print("exercises",len(h)," ".join(h))'

claims.claim: The README says the book's code samples live in chapter 1 only (附录 配套示例 links chapter 1 alone): chapter 1 is the one chapter carrying language-tagged fenced code; chapter 2's fences are unlabelled ASCII diagrams, not samples.
claims.value: 1 chapter with a language-tagged code fence — ch01-what-is-agent.md
claims.metric: chapters/*.md containing at least one ``` fence opened with a language tag (```python, ```bash, …); unlabelled fences (ASCII diagrams) do not count
claims.method: regex each chapter for a fence line that opens with a language name

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,glob,re;f=sorted(glob.glob("chapters/*.md"));h=[p.split("/")[-1] for p in f if re.search(r"^```[A-Za-z]",io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read(),re.M)];print("code-samples",len(h)," ".join(h))'

claims.claim: The hero figure numbers its five part brackets I–V as 第 1–4 / 5–6 / 7–9 / 10–11 / 12–14 章 — the same 4+2+3+2+3 split as the README's five parts, covering chapters 1–14 with no gap — and its colophon reads 14 章 · 5 部分.
claims.metric: the `part-labels` group and the `part-refs` chapter ranges plus the colophon line of assets/readme/hero.svg
claims.method: read the five `第 a–b 章` ranges out of the hero SVG, expand them and require exactly 1..14; count the part labels and the colophon's own figures

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import io,re;C=lambda *c:"".join(map(chr,c));h=io.open("assets/readme/hero.svg",encoding="utf-8").read();refs=[(int(a),int(b)) for a,b in re.findall(C(0x7b2c)+r" ([0-9]+)"+C(0x2013)+r"([0-9]+) "+C(0x7ae0),h)];lab=h.split("id=\"part-labels\"")[1].split("</g>")[0];col=re.findall("<text[^>]*>([^<]*)</text>",h.split("id=\"colophon\"")[1])[0];seq=[i for a,b in refs for i in range(a,b+1)];print("part-labels",len(re.findall(">[IVX]+</text>",lab)),"ranges",refs,"sizes",[b-a+1 for a,b in refs],"covers",len(seq),"contiguous",seq==list(range(1,15)),"colophon",[int(x) for x in re.findall("[0-9]+",col)][:2])'

expect.equals: part-labels 5 ranges [(1, 4), (5, 6), (7, 9), (10, 11), (12, 14)] sizes [4, 2, 3, 2, 3] covers 14 contiguous True colophon [14, 5]

claims.claim: Every paper the list recommends is real and still reachable at the URL given (25 links; the list's own prose cites them as the sources behind the chapters).
claims.metric: HTTP status of the 25 outbound links in references/papers.md
claims.method: fetching them needs network access, which no check in this file may do

check.manual: Needs network: reachability is an HTTP request to arxiv.org, nature.com, kaggle.com and rdi.berkeley.edu, and the claims job is deliberately offline so a dead link cannot take down the number gate. Reachability is covered by the lychee step in .github/workflows/lint.yml (references/ was added to its scope on 2026-09-12, 68 links / 0 errors). Whether each paper is the *right* recommendation for its chapter is a reading judgement no command makes.
